_comment: Scan ident (+ optional HW variant) -> definition file. The device ADDRESS is not part of this; it is taken from the scan at runtime and stamped onto the messages, so identical devices behind different bus couplers share one file. A bus coupler (e.g. V32) is only the scan key -- the file defines the device BEHIND it, distinguished by its HW variant (eloBlock vs a heat pump both scan as V32). All files are our own Apache-2.0 work: eloblock/netx3 are authored, the device types (ctlv3/pmw/vr_71/hmu/v32.hp) are re-engineered from an observed bus capture (see aioebus configs/vaillant/PROVENANCE.md). 'Broadcast' is a synthetic circuit (address 0xfe) the coordinator injects for bus broadcasts (outside temperature, date/time). 'names' maps a definition file to the friendly device name shown in Home Assistant; without an entry the scan ident is used.

models._comment: Model shown in HA, keyed by definition file. For devices behind a bus coupler the scan ident is the coupler (both the heat pump and the eloBlock scan as 'V32'); this shows the actual appliance instead.

cdn._comment: Definition file -> upstream ebus.github.io source path(s) (without the /<lang>/ prefix and .csv suffix). Used at runtime, on the user's own machine, to fetch the per-language display text and generate local translation files -- the GPL-3.0 upstream text is never stored in this repo. eloblock/netx3 are our own definitions with no upstream source.

climate._comment: Bundle per-zone registers into a climate entity (one per heating zone). For each zone N, '<prefix>N<target>' is the writable comfort setpoint (target temperature), '<prefix>N<current>' the room temperature, '<prefix>N<mode>' the operating mode (off/auto -> HVAC off/auto, others -> heat + preset). A zone is created only if it has data.

disabled_fields._comment: Entity labels ('<message> <field>') that never carried a value in the reference capture -- unconnected channels (e.g. a sensor input with nothing wired). Their sensors are created disabled by default; the user can enable them. Only affects a sensor's enabled_default at first registration.
